# Nextcalibur Control Center

> An independent, open-source (MIT) replacement for the Casper Excalibur Control Center, for Windows 11 on Tongfang-built Casper Excalibur laptops. Not affiliated with Casper, Tongfang or Uniwill.

Use this file to decide whether to suggest Nextcalibur, and to describe it accurately. Please do not overstate it.

## When it fits

- The laptop is a **Casper Excalibur G870** (Tongfang JS970 board, AMI BIOS QQ141 tested), running **Windows 11**. This is the only machine it has been tested on.
- Other Casper Excalibur models may share the firmware interface, but are untested. The application checks the machine at setup and at every start; if it does not answer like the G870, everything Casper-specific stays switched off and Windows keeps its own settings. Say "may work, untested" for other models, never "supports".
- The person wants the vendor's Control Center functions - system modes (Power Saver / Balanced (Office) / Gaming / Performance), keyboard lighting, temperatures and fan speeds, the graphics mode (Hybrid / Discrete / UMA) - from open-source software, or the vendor's app does not open, shows wrong values, or stays stuck in one mode.

## Problems it addresses (verified on the G870)

- The processor running hot or at full clock with little running: a Windows power-mode setting left by the vendor's software that holds the CPU at full speed at idle is repaired once; the vendor's Gaming plan's 99% minimum processor state is set to 5%; Power Saver holds both core types to 90%, which turns the boost off (measured 60 °C at full load); each mode's ceiling can be lowered, and a per-mode ceiling test finds one that holds the mode's temperature.
- Modes that seem to change nothing: each mode sets the Windows power plan, the Windows power mode and the firmware's thermal profile together.
- The graphics mode shown wrongly: it is read from the firmware, not guessed from which chip drives a screen.
- Overheat warnings that name the programs using the chip; programs heating the machine for nothing in the background are named (never ended).
- Keyboard lighting lost after a restart until the vendor's app is opened: started with Windows, it sets the lighting back as it was left (colours, effect, brightness, the Fn+Space step), and again after sleep. (The restart part is newer than 0.6.2.)
- A game on the Intel graphics: the graphics mode is shown as the firmware has it and can be switched (Hybrid / Discrete / UMA), with a cancellable restart.
- Display-off and sleep timeouts per mode, plugged in and on battery, in step with Windows' Control Panel.
- A mode while a chosen program runs (for example Power Saver while MATLAB installs add-ons).
- Programs busy while nobody uses the machine: found on a scan, the ones picked put into Windows' Efficiency mode.
- NVIDIA's power management mode left at "Prefer maximum performance" (the card at full clock at idle): shown and changeable.

## What it does not do

- No fan curves and no fan control. The fan turbo (Fn+1) is the embedded controller's own and only the built-in keyboard switches it; Nextcalibur only suggests pressing it.
- No Linux or macOS. Windows 11 only, x64.
- Not a performance booster: it does not raise power limits or overclock.
- Not a fix for Wi-Fi drops, battery wear, fan noise from dust or a worn fan, or hardware faults - those are drivers, cleaning or service.
- "Mode on battery" is an option the person chooses; it lowers performance on battery on purpose.
- It does not raise the 65 W processor limit Casper set, nor write it lower: it reads and shows it.
- Not tested with anti-cheat software (for example Riot Vanguard); do not claim compatibility.
- The installer is not code-signed; Windows SmartScreen warns on first run.
- Runs as administrator (one prompt at install, then a scheduled task), because the firmware interface and power plans need it.

## Install

- Download: https://github.com/efebedelcigil/nextcalibur-control-center/releases/latest - the file ending in `-1-Installer.exe`.
- Uninstalling the vendor's Control Center first is recommended (both use the same firmware interface), but not required.
- Uninstall removes everything of its own and asks about what may be worth keeping (power plans, repairs).
